justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog Management, Circulation, and User Portals fulfill cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portal requirements. However, specific mechanisms differentiating physical versus digital asset handling (e.g., digital content streaming/licensing) are only superficially mentioned.
justifications.performance_efficiency: The dedicated Elasticsearch / OpenSearch Search Container coupled with Redis Distributed Cache and token-bucket rate limiting directly guarantees achieving the sub-800ms P99 search latency requirement under high read loads.
justifications.compatibility: Standardized interoperability is well supported via OAuth2/OIDC with Identity Provider, AMQP/Kafka protocols, and RFC 7807 problem details, though library-specific bibliographic standards (e.g., MARC21, Z39.50) are not explicitly modeled.
justifications.usability: The Web Frontend includes automated WCAG accessibility testing with axe-core, and Mobile App provides offline access via Local Storage Manager. However, staff and patron user experiences are combined rather than distinctly modeled.
justifications.reliability: Reliability is well addressed through Resilience4j circuit breakers, Transactional Outbox pattern on the message broker, Spring Boot Actuator health probes, zero-downtime index alias switching, and dedicated Disaster Recovery backups.
justifications.security: Strict EU data residency is thoroughly enforced via Data Routing / Compliance Proxy, region-locked backup targets, localized OTel PII sanitization, OAuth2/OIDC identity management, and secure local keychain storage.
justifications.maintainability: Microservice decomposition isolates domain logic into Catalog Management, Circulation, and User Portals. AsyncAPI schema registry, centralized configuration via Consul, and standardized error handling maximize testability and modifiability.
justifications.portability: The architecture specifies OCI-compliant containers across all services, standardized NGINX/Envoy ingress, and Spring Boot runtimes, enabling seamless portability across any EU-compliant cloud provider or on-premise infrastructure.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture explicitly incorporates a dedicated Elasticsearch/OpenSearch search container paired with a Redis distributed cache and API Gateway caching layer designed specifically to meet the sub-800ms P99 search requirement under high concurrency.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch cluster sizing and index shard distribution
tradeoffs: In-memory cache footprint cost versus low query response latency

PERF-02.justification: Updates write to isolated databases and broadcast events via RabbitMQ/Kafka, asynchronously updating Elasticsearch and invalidating Redis caches via listeners without blocking search query paths, easily achieving visibility well within 5 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Asynchronous indexing throughput and broker consumer lag under peak load
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of searchable items versus unhindered write and search throughput

AVAIL-01.justification: Circulation is decoupled into an independent microservice with its own database and transactional outbox, protecting loan transactions. Elasticsearch index management handles alias routing, though explicit multi-node replica clustering details for OpenSearch are minimally specified.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch replica shard configuration and automatic master failover duration
tradeoffs: Hardware overhead of replica shards versus search availability guarantees

AVAIL-02.justification: User Portals are stateless Spring Boot containers with Actuator health probes and externalized session storage in Redis. The API Gateway detects failed instances via probes and routes traffic immediately to healthy instances without dropping transactions.
sensitivity_points: Health probe polling interval and failure detection threshold at the API Gateway
tradeoffs: Frequent health probe network overhead versus faster failure detection

MOD-01.justification: Catalog Management is a single Spring Boot component without explicit extension points, adapter layers, or modular connector components for external content providers. Adding an e-book provider requires modifying the core Catalog Management service codebase directly.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between external provider data structures and core catalog models
tradeoffs: Monolithic catalog component simplicity versus modular adapter extensibility

MOD-02.justification: The architecture provides a Centralized Configuration Store (Spring Cloud Config and Consul) designed to serve externalized configurations dynamically without redeployment. However, explicit runtime rule engine abstractions within the Circulation component are not detailed.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic configuration reload mechanism and runtime schema validation in Circulation
tradeoffs: Dynamic configuration flexibility versus potential runtime validation errors

SEC-01.justification: Strict EU data residency is designed into every layer: a dedicated Data Routing/Compliance Proxy filters traffic, databases and backup targets are explicitly region-locked to the EU, and log agents sanitize PII before external aggregation.
sensitivity_points: Accuracy and maintenance of geographic routing policies and geo-IP lookup rules
tradeoffs: Proxy inspection and enforcement latency versus absolute regulatory compliance

SEC-02.justification: Authentication is governed via OAuth2/OIDC tokens at the API Gateway and downstream services, while unauthorized access triggers RFC 7807 problem details and audit logging via the telemetry agent. However, explicit patron-to-record authorization policies are only generically implied.
sensitivity_points: Granular enforcement of object-level authorization rules based on JWT claims
tradeoffs: Fine-grained access evaluation processing overhead versus coarse-grained role checks
